title: The Verdict of the Fens
premise: Retired detective Ines Halloran, now barely keeping her fen-edge bookshop afloat, is handed the diary of a woman who vanished three years ago—only to find entries written after her disappearance. Following the diary's trail, Ines uncovers a web of silence in the marsh town of Wraybourne, where a powerful family's annual dinner marks the anniversary of a drowning no one wants examined. As Ines closes in on a witness the town swears is dead, she must choose between protecting the one person loyal to her and exposing the truth. At the anniversary dinner, she forces a public reckoning: the missing woman is alive, hidden by the town itself, and justice arrives outside any courtroom.
about_author: Noor Eastwick is a former court reporter who spent a decade covering small-town inquests in the East Anglian fens before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep to survive.

chapters.title: Waterlogged Pages
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A stranger leaves a sodden diary on the bookshop counter and vanishes into the rain. Ines recognizes the handwriting of Maren Dusk, declared drowned three years ago. The last entry is dated two months after her disappearance. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity reigniting a dormant instinct.

chapters.title: The Shop That Won't Sell
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Flashbacks weave through a slow day of failed sales and overdue rent, establishing her unsolved-case shame and why she retired. She tells herself to hand the diary to police. She doesn't. Emotional beat: loneliness and the pull of unfinished business.

chapters.title: Entries Past the End
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Reading the diary through the night, Ines finds coded references to places only locals know: the sluice gate, the chapel ruin, the eel sheds. The final entry names a date—the anniversary dinner. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wraybourne Remembers Nothing
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines visits Wraybourne, where Maren drowned, and finds a town of polished grief and shut doors. The Ashcombe family, whose dinner marks the anniversary, is revered. Emotional beat: the uncanny warmth of a place hiding something cold.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Watches
chapters.summary: Sorrel Ashcombe's POV. The matriarch of the Ashcombe family notes a stranger asking questions and makes quiet calls. Her loyalty to her family's name is absolute. Emotional beat: menace wrapped in hospitality.

chapters.title: The Constable's Debt
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines approaches DC Ferren, once her protégé, who owes her his career. He confirms the drowning verdict was rushed but begs her to drop it. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning to fracture under the weight of truth.

chapters.title: Eel Sheds at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the diary's clues to the eel sheds, Ines finds a hidden cache: Maren's spare clothes, a train timetable, and a second notebook with pages torn out. Someone was watching her that night too. Emotional beat: the case turning from disappearance to conspiracy.

chapters.title: What the Ferryman Saw
chapters.summary: New POV: Tolly, an elderly ferryman. He recalls the night Maren 'drowned'—a boat with two passengers, one of them wearing Ashcombe colors. He's never told anyone. Emotional beat: fear finally cracking after three years of silence.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Preparations for the dinner proceed, but Sorrel discovers someone has been asking about the chapel ruin. She orders her son Cass to handle it 'the family way.' Emotional beat: power flexing, corruption normalized as duty.

chapters.title: Cass Ashcombe's Conscience
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass, who loved Maren once, is ordered to intimidate Ines. He warns her off instead—and lets slip that Maren had proof of something the family buried: a pollution cover-up that killed a farmworker. Emotional beat: guilt turning a loyal son into a liability.

chapters.title: Torn Pages, Whole Truths
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The torn pages from the second notebook resurface, mailed anonymously: Maren documented the cover-up, and the 'drowning' was her staged escape—until someone tried to make it real. Emotional beat: the mystery inverting—Maren isn't a victim of murder but a fugitive from it.

chapters.title: Ferren's Report
chapters.summary: Ferren's POV. Ordered by his superiors to surveil Ines, Ferren files false reports instead, buying her time. He knows it ends his career either way. Emotional beat: loyalty choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: The Chapel Ruin
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. At the ruin, Ines finds fresh candle wax and a message scratched in Latin: 'The dead keep accounts.' Maren has been living in the fens all along, moving between hides. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: A Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Ines and Maren's shared scene. Maren finally appears—gaunt, wary, armed with three years of evidence. She trusts no one, least of all the law that ruled her dead. Ines must convince her the dinner is the moment to surface. Emotional beat: two stubborn women negotiating trust.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Sorrel learns Maren lives and orders a final cleanup before the dinner, framing the ferryman Tolly for Maren's 'murder.' Emotional beat: the mask of respectability dropping entirely.

chapters.title: Tolly Taken
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Tolly is arrested; the town closes ranks. Ines realizes the frame will stick unless Maren appears publicly—tonight, at the dinner, where every witness and every enemy will be in one room. Emotional beat: the trap becoming the stage.

chapters.title: Dressing for a Funeral
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren prepares to walk into the house that tried to erase her, wearing her old identity like armor. Ines gives her the diary back—the original, the one thing Sorrel wants destroyed. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Toasts are raised to Maren's memory as she walks in alive. Sorrel's composure shatters; Cass refuses to back his mother; Ferren arrives with the evidence file. Emotional beat: the glass raised to a lie, and the lie dying mid-toast.

chapters.title: Confession at the Head of the Table
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Sorrel, cornered before the assembled town, confesses the cover-up and the attempt on Maren's life—recording devices running, courtesy of Ferren. Emotional beat: justice delivered not by court but by community witness.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Marsh
chapters.summary: Ferren's POV. Arrests ripple outward; Ferren turns in his badge expecting ruin and is instead asked to consult on reopening old cases. Maren declines the spotlight, evidence speaking for her. Emotional beat: the law, humbled, reaching back toward justice.

chapters.title: The Shop That Sells Again
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop thrives on newfound notoriety. Maren visits, alive and unhidden, and leaves a new diary on the counter—blank, a gift. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Ines's final POV. Standing at the sluice gate where it began, Ines reflects on loyalty, truth, and the town that chose both. She closes her last unsolved case file and opens the blank diary. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—the fens keep their dead, but not their secrets.
